context.title: A Bride for Isaac
context.summary: Abraham's servant travels to Abraham's relatives in Mesopotamia to find a wife for Isaac, prays for a sign at the well, and meets Rebekah, who agrees to return with him and marry Isaac.
context.background: This is the longest chapter in Genesis. Marriages were arranged between families, often within the wider clan. Watering ten thirsty camels (vv. 10, 19) meant drawing a great deal of water by hand.

customs.note: A solemn oath gesture, used again by Jacob (47:29). Its exact meaning is uncertain; many connect it to the life and descendants of the one receiving the oath.

watchFor: The servant's prayer is answered before he has finished speaking (v. 15).
The whole story is retold to Rebekah's family (vv. 34–49).

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

people.name: Isaac
people.summary: The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3).

people.name: Rebekah
people.summary: A noose, the daughter of Bethuel, and the wife of Isaac (Gen. 22:23; 24:67). The circumstances under which Abraham’s “steward” found her at the “city of Nahor,” in Padan-aram, are narrated in Gen. 24-27.

people.name: Nahor
people.summary: A son of Terah, and elder brother of Abraham (Gen. 11:26, 27; Josh. 24:2, R.V.). He married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran, and remained in the land of his nativity on the east of the river Euphrates at Haran (Gen. 11:27-32).

people.name: Bethuel
people.summary: The son of Nahor by Milcah; nephew of Abraham, and father of Rebekah (Gen. 22:22, 23; 24:15, 24, 47).

people.name: Laban
people.summary: The son of Bethuel, who was the son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. He lived at Haran in Mesopotamia. His sister Rebekah was Isaac’s wife (Gen. 24).

people.name: Sarah
people.summary: Princess, the wife and at the same time the half-sister of Abraham (Gen. 11:29; 20:12). This name was given to her at the time that it was announced to Abraham that she should be the mother of the promised child.

places.name: Mesopotamia
places.summary: The country between the two rivers (Heb. Aram-naharaim; i.e., “Syria of the two rivers”), the name given by the Greeks and Romans to the region between the Euphrates and the Tigris (Gen. 24:10; Deut. 23:4; Judg. 3:8, 10).

places.name: Beer-lahai-roi
places.summary: I.e., “the well of him that liveth and seeth me,” or, as some render it, “the well of the vision of life”, the well where the Lord met with Hagar (Gen. 16:7-14).

places.name: Negeb
places.summary: Heb. Negeb, that arid district to the south of Palestine through which lay the caravan route from Central Palestine to Egypt (Gen. 12:9; 13:1, 3; 46:1-6).
